The core derivation involves constructing a sequence of probability spaces (Xn, Sn, μn) and forming their product space (X, S). The set function μ is defined on a field F such that each restriction μ|Fn is a probability measure. Absolute continuity ensures that μ admits a unique extension to the full σ-algebra S. This structure enables recursive conditioning and probabilistic inference in complex domains. Dualities arise between conditional probabilities and marginal distributions, especially when considering transformations Tn(x). Failure modes occur when absolute continuity breaks down, causing μ to not extend uniquely or at all. These primitives support both Bayesian updating and state transition dynamics in GSE.
